system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Communication and interpersonal skills, including health literacy and numeracy, cultural competence
Patient interviewing, consultation, and interactions with the family (patient-centered communication skills)
diagnosis: Effective communication accommodation for a patient with a vision disability
mechanism: Federal disability-rights requirements call for communication with patients with vision disabilities to be as effective as communication with others. When necessary, covered health programs should provide appropriate auxiliary aids or services such as qualified readers, Braille, large print, or accessible electronic formats, with the choice guided by effective communication and the individual's needs.
vignette: At an outpatient clinic that receives federal financial assistance, a 63-year-old woman with severe visual impairment is being counseled about a new long-term medication. She independently manages her health decisions but cannot read the standard-print medication instructions. She asks for the information in an electronic format compatible with her screen reader.
lead: Which response by the clinic is most appropriate?
correct: Provide the instructions in an accessible electronic format that permits effective communication
distractors: Require a family member to read the standard-print instructions to her
Provide the standard-print instructions because the same document is given to all patients
Ask her to sign a waiver stating that written instructions cannot be provided
Withhold written information and rely only on a brief verbal summary
distractor_notes: A support person does not remove the covered entity's responsibility to ensure effective communication when an auxiliary aid or accessible format is needed.
Providing identical inaccessible material does not make communication equally effective for a patient with a vision disability.
The appropriate response is to furnish an effective auxiliary aid or accessible format rather than shift the accessibility burden to the patient.
The nature and complexity of the communication matter; an accessible format can provide the same information independently rather than unnecessarily limiting the patient to a shortened summary.
key_expl: HHS disability-rights rules require covered health programs to take appropriate steps to ensure communication with people with vision disabilities is as effective as communication with others. Auxiliary aids and services can include Braille, large print, qualified readers, and accessible electronic information usable with a screen reader.
objective: Apply disability-access principles by selecting an effective accessible format for a patient with visual impairment rather than relying on family members, inaccessible standard print, waivers, or reduced information.

outline: Diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the endocrine pancreas
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Pathogenic variants in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2 impair adipocyte development or function and prevent normal storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue. The resulting near-total loss of body fat causes ectopic lipid deposition, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, and fatty liver.
vignette: A 15-year-old boy has had an unusually muscular appearance with almost no visible subcutaneous fat since infancy. Examination shows hepatomegaly and acanthosis nigricans. Laboratory studies show severe hypertriglyceridemia and fasting hyperglycemia. His parents are clinically unaffected.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?
distractor_notes: Familial hypercholesterolemia causes markedly elevated LDL cholesterol and premature atherosclerosis, not near-total absence of adipose tissue with ectopic fat storage and severe insulin resistance.
Glycogen storage disease type I produces fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and metabolic abnormalities but does not cause congenital generalized loss of adipose tissue.
Cushing syndrome causes centripetal fat accumulation rather than a congenital near-total absence of adipose tissue.
Prader-Willi syndrome is characterized by hyperphagia and obesity rather than generalized congenital lipodystrophy.
key_expl: Congenital generalized lipodystrophy is characterized by an almost total absence of adipose tissue from birth or early childhood. Defects in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2 impair adipocyte lipid storage, causing ectopic lipid deposition, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, and hepatic steatosis.
objective: Recognize congenital generalized lipodystrophy from near-total loss of adipose tissue with a muscular appearance, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance, and hepatomegaly.
clues: near-total absence of subcutaneous fat since infancy

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease due to PLP1 dysfunction
mechanism: PLP1 variants disrupt proteolipid protein 1/DM20 production, folding, trafficking, or availability in oligodendrocyte membranes. Because these proteins are major components of central nervous system myelin, the result is hypomyelination and progressive neurologic dysfunction, usually in males with X-linked inheritance.
vignette: A 10-month-old boy has persistent nystagmus, delayed motor development, hypotonia, and progressive difficulty controlling head and trunk movements. Brain MRI shows diffuse hypomyelination. His maternal uncle had a similar childhood neurologic disorder.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Alexander disease is a GFAP-related leukodystrophy characterized by abnormal astroglial Rosenthal fibers rather than the classic X-linked PLP1 hypomyelination pattern.
Krabbe disease is caused by GALC deficiency with toxic galactolipid accumulation and demyelination, not PLP1-related hypomyelination.
Canavan disease results from aspartoacylase deficiency and N-acetylaspartate accumulation rather than an X-linked myelin structural-protein defect.
Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a lysosomal sulfatide-storage disorder rather than the PLP1-associated X-linked hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
key_expl: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease is an X-linked leukodystrophy caused by PLP1 variants. Proteolipid protein 1 and DM20 are major components of CNS myelin; abnormal production or trafficking leads to hypomyelination, nystagmus, motor delay, and progressive neurologic impairment in affected males.
objective: Recognize Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease from early nystagmus, motor delay, diffuse hypomyelination, and an X-linked family pattern.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Renal coloboma syndrome (papillorenal syndrome) due to PAX2 dysfunction
mechanism: PAX2 encodes a transcription factor required for normal embryonic development of the kidneys and eyes. Loss of functional PAX2 can disrupt formation of renal tissue and the optic nerve, producing congenital kidney abnormalities with optic nerve coloboma; inheritance is autosomal dominant when a pathogenic PAX2 variant is present.
vignette: A 17-year-old boy is evaluated for slowly progressive chronic kidney disease. Renal ultrasonography shows bilaterally small, hypoplastic kidneys. Ophthalmologic examination shows bilateral optic nerve colobomas. His father has chronic kidney disease and a congenital optic nerve abnormality.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this combination of renal and ocular findings?
distractor_notes: Alport syndrome is a hereditary type IV collagen disorder classically associated with hematuric kidney disease, sensorineural hearing loss, and ocular abnormalities rather than bilateral optic nerve colobomas with hypoplastic kidneys.

Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease causes progressive formation of numerous renal cysts with kidney enlargement rather than congenital optic nerve colobomas and bilaterally hypoplastic kidneys.

Tuberous sclerosis complex causes multisystem benign tumors, including renal tumors, together with characteristic neurologic and skin manifestations; it does not produce the PAX2-pattern combination of optic nerve coloboma and renal hypoplasia.

Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease is typically apparent at birth or in early infancy and is characterized by cystic kidney disease, not this autosomal-dominant optic-nerve-coloboma and renal-hypoplasia phenotype.
key_expl: Renal coloboma syndrome is caused by pathogenic PAX2 variants in many affected families. PAX2 is a transcription factor involved in embryonic kidney and eye development; loss of function can produce renal hypoplasia or other congenital renal abnormalities together with optic nerve coloboma.
objective: Recognize renal coloboma syndrome from congenital kidney disease plus optic nerve coloboma and connect the phenotype to PAX2-dependent embryonic development.

outline: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders, including microbiologic and host response to insult
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Hailey-Hailey disease due to ATP2C1 dysfunction
mechanism: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered pump that transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi apparatus. Loss of functional hSPCA1 disrupts Golgi calcium storage in keratinocytes, impairing cell adhesion and making the epidermis fragile in areas exposed to heat, moisture, and friction.
vignette: A 27-year-old woman has recurrent painful, raw, blistered plaques in the axillae and groin that worsen with heat and sweating. Her father has had similar episodes since early adulthood. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in ATP2C1.
lead: The protein encoded by the mutated gene normally performs which cellular function?
correct: ATP-dependent transport of calcium into the Golgi apparatus
distractors: ATP-dependent transport of calcium into the endoplasmic reticulum
Voltage-gated transport of calcium into cells across the plasma membrane
ATP-dependent transport of copper within the Golgi and into biliary secretory vesicles
Channel-mediated transport of chloride across the plasma membrane
distractor_notes: SERCA2, encoded by ATP2A2, is an ATP-dependent calcium pump of the endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum. ATP2C1 instead encodes hSPCA1, which pumps calcium into the Golgi apparatus.
CaV1.2, encoded by CACNA1C, is a voltage-gated plasma-membrane calcium channel that permits calcium entry into cells; it is not the ATP2C1-encoded Golgi ATPase.
ATP7B is a copper-transporting P-type ATPase that functions in the Golgi and can traffic to vesicles for biliary copper elimination; ATP2C1 instead transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi.
CFTR is a plasma-membrane chloride channel; it does not perform ATP-dependent sequestration of calcium into the Golgi.
key_expl: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered calcium pump that transports calcium into the Golgi apparatus. Reduced hSPCA1 activity impairs Golgi calcium storage, disrupts keratinocyte adhesion, and produces the recurrent flexural blistering of Hailey-Hailey disease.
objective: Connect Hailey-Hailey disease caused by ATP2C1 variants to defective ATP-dependent calcium transport into the Golgi apparatus.
